summary: Order lifecycle state machine with a Fastify API and a passing happy-path vitest suite; canTransition lets an unpaid order go straight from created to shipped.

defects.summary: canTransition allows created -> shipped because the 'shipped' case only checks from !== 'shipped' instead of from === 'paid', so an unpaid order can be shipped (README: an order must be paid before it can be shipped).
defects.observable: canTransition('created', 'shipped') returns true (expected false); transition(createOrder(...), 'shipped', now) succeeds instead of throwing InvalidTransitionError. Over HTTP: POST /orders {customerId:'c_1', totalCents:4999} -> 201, then POST /orders/<id>/transitions {to:'shipped'} -> 200 with status 'shipped' instead of 409 invalid_transition. This is the only invalid transition that is accepted: created->delivered, cancelled->shipped, shipped->shipped, shipped->cancelled, shipped->paid and anything out of delivered/cancelled correctly return 409.

notDefects: created -> cancelled and paid -> cancelled are allowed by design
delivered and cancelled are terminal; 409 for any transition out of them is correct
Malformed order ids (non UUID) return 400 by design, unknown ids 404
Repeating the current status (e.g. paid -> paid) returns 409 by design
Orders are stored in memory; there is no authentication by design
mustNotReport: Do not report cancelled -> shipped, shipped -> cancelled or delivered -> anything as accepted; they are correctly rejected with 409
Do not report a failing test suite: all 6 existing tests pass
Do not report 409 responses for invalid transitions as product defects
